subject: QBR prep: exec asks, roadmap exceptions & cross-func follow-ups
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: exec asks, roadmap exceptions & cross-func follow-ups

Team — thanks for a productive weekly sync. Recap and explicit owners below so we have a clean QBR playbook by next week. Please confirm owners/ETAs by EOD Friday.

1) Exec asks collection (Ben / Laura) — Ben: pull together the four high-priority asks that need exec sign-off for QBR. Deliverable: one-page summary with one-line impact and ask. ETA: 2027-06-01.

2) Exception register follow-ups (Marissa) — Marissa: review the open exceptions from roadmap (latency > target for short sequences; Dedicated capacity autoscale gaps). Action: add root cause and mitigation note in exception_register.csv and tag owner. ETA: 2027-05-31.

3) Model rollout compatibility (Karthik) — Identify top 2 kernel/quantization risks that could force fallback during canary. Action: propose fallback pairing and timeline with Research. ETA: 2027-05-30.

4) Production guardrails (Vivek) — Confirm SLO rollback thresholds and canary window for the QBR demo traffic pattern. Deliverable: Runbook stub + brief. ETA: 2027-05-29.

Notes / risks:
- Customer (Acme Analytics) wants a canary demo the week after QBR; we must avoid last-minute rollouts.
- We may need a short SLA exception for Dedicated during the demo traffic spike — Laura please advise.

Attachments: QBR_prompt_set_v2.xlsx (prompt/eval set); exception_register.csv (tracker)

Thanks — please keep replies inline where you update an ETA.

Ben Carter
Sales Director | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
(415) 555-0184

Ben — thanks for the clear breakdown. Quick updates inline and one change of owners: 

> 1) Exec asks collection (Ben / Laura) — Ben: pull together the four high-priority asks that need exec sign-off for QBR.
- + Confirmed. I will add the ask that impacts the Acme demo (priority 1) into the one-pager draft so it's visible.

> 2) Exception register follow-ups (Marissa) — Marissa: review the open exceptions from roadmap (latency > target for short sequences; Dedicated capacity autoscale gaps).
- Done: I started the exception_register.csv and flagged 3 rows as P1 (latency short-seq, autoscale config, KV cache invalidation). Assigning leads: Infra (Rohan) for autoscale; Runtime (Sofia) for KV cache; Performance (Marcus) for latency tuning. I'll email owners separately and attach a short mitigation plan.

> 3) Model rollout compatibility (Karthik) — Identify top 2 kernel/quantization risks that could force fallback during canary.
- Karthik: noted. I put a placeholder in the exceptions file referencing the canary fallback playbook. See attached.

> 4) Production guardrails (Vivek) — Confirm SLO rollback thresholds and canary window for the QBR demo traffic pattern.
- Vivek: can you confirm whether we want 5% error budget burn in 10m or 15m? My recommendation is 10m for the demo.

I've attached the canary_fallback_playbook.pdf (short playbook + contact list). I'll update the tracker with owners & links by EOD Friday.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachment: canary_fallback_playbook.pdf

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: QBR prep: exec asks, roadmap exceptions & cross-func follow-ups

Quick product follow-up after digging into the exception rows Marissa created. Key asks for the one-pager and owners: 

1) Kernel/quantization risk (owner: Research - Priya) — Two models in the catalog use recently-introduced INT4 paths; latency looks fine locally but may fail under the QBR demo token patterns because of attention matrix tiling. Ask: Research to validate the INT4 path under demo config + provide fallback variant (INT8 / fp16) that is pre-compiled by 2027-05-31.

2) Autoscale warmup (owner: Infra - Rohan) — Current autoscale policy does not pre-warm GPU pool for short high-burst demos (observed at customer PoCs). Ask: add a temporary pre-warm policy for the Acme demo week and document rollback. ETA for policy change: 2027-05-29.

Action items I'm taking on: update the model compatibility row in exception_register.csv with the exact test matrix I want Research to run and add quantization fallback mapping.

One operational ask for leadership: if we expect demo traffic > 50k tokens/min, we should approve a short Dedicated burst window as part of the QBR plan (approx cost estimate attached in the QBR doc). Laura — can you confirm permission for a 48-hour burst window if needed?

Thanks — I'll sync with Priya and Rohan this afternoon.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Product | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

All — thanks for the quick turn. I reviewed the one-pager draft Ben referenced (looks good); a few leadership notes: 

- Mark the kernel/quantization row and autoscale pre-warm as "Exec Ask" items in the one-pager. These are showstoppers for the Acme demo and need explicit buy-in.
- I approve a 48-hour Dedicated burst window for the QBR demo contingent on a rollback plan and cost cap (Marissa, include cost cap in the QBR doc).
- Karthik: Research + Infra should own the testing and the playbook. Priya and Rohan, please coordinate and post results to the shared Drive folder below by 2027-05-31.

I've created a canonical QBR folder and added a stub deck — please add a one-slide summary of your ask under /Exec-Asks. Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QBRdoc_example

Marissa — treat the Acme demo as the priority exception; label it P0 in exception_register.csv. I'll escalate to CTO if we don't have validated fallbacks by the 31st.

I'll be at the QBR readout; let's get the one-pager in place early next week so execs have time to review.

Laura Bennett
VP, GTM Operations | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

Cc: Julia Sanders (Acme) and CloudX to keep them informed of the plan and timeline.
